title: Common-field descent of exceptional adjunction maps and evaluation
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ separated of finite type. For finite intermediate fields $E\subset\Omega$ use the rationalized constructible categories $\mathcal C_{T,E}=D^b_c(T,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and scalar extension $T^T_{L/E}$. Use their common-stage pair categories $\mathcal C_{T,\Omega}$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]: objects are $(E,K)$ and Hom groups are directed colimits over common finite fields, with composition represented at a common field. Write $F_E=Rf_{!,E}$, $G_E=Rf_E^!$, and $H_{T,E}=R\mathcal Hom_E$ for the coefficient-passage operations [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Suppose the finite-field adjunctions $F_E\dashv G_E$, internal Hom and tensor have coherent scalar-extension comparisons preserving their units $\eta_E$, counits $\epsilon_E$ and evaluations $\operatorname{ev}_E$; coherent means the comparisons are the identity at equal fields and agree for successive field inclusions, including tensor associators.

The induced common-stage functors have a natural adjunction whose Hom bijection, for $K=(E,K_E)$ and $M=(E',M_{E'})$, is
$$\varinjlim_{L\supset E,E'}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_{Y,L}}(F_LK_L,M_L)\ \cong\ \varinjlim_{L\supset E,E'}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_{X,L}}(K_L,G_LM_L),$$
where $K_L=T^X_{L/E}K_E$ and $M_L=T^Y_{L/E'}M_{E'}$, and each transition uses the specified operation comparisons. Its unit at $(E,K_E)$ is the class $[E,\eta_{E,K_E}]$ and its counit at $(E,M_E)$ is $[E,\epsilon_{E,M_E}]$. For objects $P=(E,P_E)$, $Q=(E',Q_{E'})$ on $T$, the evaluation $H_{T,\Omega}(P,Q)\otimes P\to Q$ is the class $[L,\operatorname{ev}_{L,P_L,Q_L}]$, with sources and targets identified by the specified comparisons. These formulas are independent of the common field and of the representatives, natural for all common-stage arrows, and preserve the finite-stage normalization of the maps. The two triangle identities, and every finite diagram equality built from these maps and the specified comparisons that holds at a common finite stage, hold in the colimit Hom groups. No finite-quotient reduction on $\mathcal C_{T,\Omega}$ is asserted.

proof.text: Use StageSystem.Morphism.descNatTrans on the finite units and counits. The supplied unit and counit transition equations are exactly Hom.comm for the identity and composite stage-system morphisms. Compose with functorIdIso and functorCompIso, whose components are identities. Their descended components are the stage-inclusion images of the finite components.

Use Adjunction.mkOfUnitCounit. Both triangles follow by functor_map_ι and preservation of composition from the finite triangle identities. For the two representative formulas expand homEquiv_unit/homEquiv_counit, represent the descended component at the chosen common stage by ι_map_eq, and apply functor_map_mkHom and mkHom_comp_mkHom. The unit transition equation gives the forward formula; the counit transition equation and cancellation of inverse beta comparisons give the inverse formula.

On each scheme transport the base-field unit for ell to every residue field. Specialize PodCommonTransposeNormalization for podCommonClosed to the Hom object and its identity; use the operation object equality from commonStageDerivedInternalHom_existsUnique to identify the literal representative. This proves the evaluation representative clause. Apply lem-sf-common-stage-evaluation-naturality to its naturality clause.
